lead.title: Man & Science implants all 10 patients in ONFIELD, the first-in-human study of its miniaturised occipital nerve stimulator
lead.deck: The Liège-based medtech has implanted and activated all ten planned patients in ONFIELD, the first-in-human study of its occipital nerve stimulation (ONS) implant — no implanted battery, no tunnelled leads — for chronic cluster headache: early signs of fewer attacks and no serious device-related adverse events. Next step: preparing the pivotal phase for a programme already holding FDA Breakthrough Device designation — a Walloon startup (Noshaq, Wallonie Entreprendre) to track ahead of its next round.

milestone.title: Implantica performs its first US RefluxStop implantations following PMA approval
milestone.summary: Three months after FDA PMA approval (Aug 20, 2026), the first US procedures with RefluxStop — an anti-reflux implant that restores anatomy without compressing the oesophagus — were performed in early November by Dr John Lipham at USC. Q3 sales jumped 105% (€748K), with €38.3M in cash.
milestone.why: A European medtech clearing PMA and then treating its first US patient shows the FDA's most demanding pathway is still reachable from Europe; the US adoption curve will be the real valuation test for gastrointestinal implants.

brefsEurope.title: Haemonetics wins CE mark (MDR) for VASCADE MVP XL femoral venous closure
brefsEurope.summary: The venous vascular closure system, designed for 10–12F sheaths (PFA, cryoablation, LAA closure), is certified under MDR; first European procedures took place in October in Hamburg, Milan and London. Comparable: the PFA boom is lifting the whole vascular-access accessory ecosystem.

brefsEurope.title: Siemens Healthineers secures FDA 510(k) for syngo.CT Coronary Cockpit, an AI coronary plaque analysis tool
brefsEurope.summary: The software quantifies and characterises coronary plaque from CCTA scans using AI segmentation, to stratify risk and help plan PCI. Market signal: the majors are moving into plaque analysis, turf of cardiac AI startups.

brefsEurope.title: Abbott launches VOYAGER CE trial of its software-guided balloon-expandable Encantor TAVI
brefsEurope.summary: The single-arm pre-market study will enrol up to 300 patients in Europe and Australia; Dr Didier Tchétché (Clinique Pasteur, Toulouse) is co-principal investigator. Abbott is taking on the Edwards-dominated balloon-expandable TAVI segment, with Europe as its first gateway.

brefsEurope.title: MedUni Vienna spin-off Exalt wins the 15th MEDICA Start-up Competition
brefsEurope.summary: Its functional oncology platform tests a patient's tumour cells against more than 100 cancer drugs and returns a ranked treatment profile in ~72 hours (haematological malignancies). Also on the podium: Paracly (Cologne), medical-device cybersecurity, 2nd place and public vote.

brefsEurope.title: Romania's .lumen wins the 18th Healthcare Innovation World Cup with its navigation glasses for the blind
brefsEurope.summary: The AI glasses detect obstacles and walkable paths and guide the user through haptic feedback; .lumen also took the public vote. Belgium's Allow Motion (Seraing, 3D-printed NeoHand myoelectric hand) came third.

brefsEurope.title: Primedea raises a pre-seed round led by Hansi Hansmann for its teleradiology network
brefsEurope.summary: The Zurich startup runs a network of radiologists for remote reporting of imaging studies; the round (undisclosed amount) is led by Austrian business angel Hansi Hansmann. A response to Europe's radiologist shortage.

brefsIntl.title: Biostream receives Breakthrough Device Designation for a urine test for normal pressure hydrocephalus
brefsIntl.summary: Founded in 2025, the startup measures a urinary protein panel and outputs a probability score to tell idiopathic normal pressure hydrocephalus apart from Alzheimer's in people over 60 (designation granted Nov 12). A non-invasive diagnostic for a potentially reversible dementia.

brefsIntl.title: BURL Concepts wins FDA 510(k) for FOQUS, an automated transcranial ultrasound for PFO screening
brefsIntl.summary: The low-frequency ultrasound headset scans the brain in ~40 seconds to detect right-to-left shunts (patent foramen ovale) and can be run by a single nurse. Already used in the Netherlands and the UK under CE mark; US launch in early 2027.

word.definition: A therapy that places a small electrode next to a peripheral nerve (occipital, tibial, back or cranial nerves) and sends it weak electrical pulses to modulate pain or a function, without drugs.

parts.label: Electrode
parts.role: the contact right next to the target nerve

parts.label: Generator / antenna
parts.role: the power source, increasingly external (no implanted battery)

parts.label: Programming
parts.role: tuning the pulses to each patient

how.t: The physician identifies the responsible nerve (e.g. the occipital nerve in cluster headache) and places the electrode through an incision or a minimally invasive injection.
An implanted generator or, in recent devices, an external unit worn on the skin powers the implant through the tissue.
The electrical pulses alter nerve signal transmission, reducing the frequency or intensity of pain attacks.

word.why: PNS is shrinking: with no implanted battery or tunnelled leads, surgery gets lighter and devices easier to roll out. The majors are consolidating the segment (Medtronic bought SPR Therapeutics, Boston Scientific bought Nalu), creating clear exit paths for European startups still in the clinic for headache and migraine.

startups.name: Man & Science
startups.use: Miniaturised occipital stimulation implant for chronic cluster headache; ONFIELD study (10 patients) fully implanted, FDA Breakthrough designation

startups.name: Salvia BioElectronics
startups.use: MySalvia system (two ultra-thin implants under the scalp) for migraine; first US patient in the randomised RECLAIM-II trial in October 2026

startups.name: Neuronoff
startups.use: Injectrode, a minimally invasive injectable electrode for PNS; first patient in a DoD-funded trial (neurogenic bladder), 510(k) submission targeted in 2026

startups.name: Curonix
startups.use: Freedom PNS system with no implanted battery (510(k) K233162), extended to chronic craniofacial pain in 2026
